task: Verify a published claim about the effect of BERC Reconsideration Order 2026/01 (4 June 2026) on residential electricity bills in Bangladesh.
context:
BERC Order 2026/22 of 3 June 2026 set the BPDB LT-A residential ladder as: lifeline (0-50 units) Tk 5.32/kWh; first step (0-75 units) Tk 6.18; second step (76-200) Tk 8.50; third (201-300) Tk 9.10; fourth (301-400) Tk 9.62; fifth (401-600) Tk 15.01; sixth (above 600) Tk 17.35. Demand charge Tk 42.00 per kW of sanctioned load per month.

BERC Reconsideration Order 2026/01 of 4 June 2026 restored the lifeline to Tk 4.63 and the first step to Tk 5.26, effective from the same bill month (June 2026), and left every other row unchanged.

Slab semantics, from footnote 3 of both the June 2026 notification and gazette S.R.O. 43-Law/2024: the lifeline is CATEGORICAL - the 0-50 rate applies to all consumption but only if total monthly consumption is 50 units or less; a consumer above 50 units receives none of it and billing begins at the 0-75 first step. All other steps are TELESCOPIC - only the units falling inside the band are priced at that band's rate.

VAT and any prompt-payment rebate are UNKNOWN: no instrument held states the VAT base for the energy or demand charge, so no bill total can currently be computed. Only the energy charge is calculable.

claims.claim: The 4 June reconsideration reduced every residential bill in the country by Tk 69.00 relative to the 3 June order.
claims.basis: The first step (0-75) is telescopic, so it prices the first 75 units of every bill; 75 x (6.18 - 5.26) = Tk 69.00.

claims.claim: Below 75 units the reduction is larger than Tk 69.00.
claims.basis: Low-consumption households were the stated beneficiaries of the reconsideration.

claims.claim: The 4 June reconsideration was not relief confined to low-income households; it changed what consumers above 75 units pay as well.
claims.basis: Only the lifeline row is categorical; the first step is telescopic and therefore reaches every residential bill.

arithmetic.statement: Under the governing (post-4-June) schedule, 50 kWh costs Tk 231.50 and 51 kWh costs Tk 268.26.
arithmetic.shownWorking: 50 x 4.63 = 231.50 (lifeline applies). 51 > 50, so the lifeline is lost entirely and all 51 units price at the first step: 51 x 5.26 = 268.26.

arithmetic.statement: Under the governing schedule, 412 kWh has an energy charge of Tk 3,509.12.
Under the 3 June schedule, 412 kWh has an energy charge of Tk 3,578.12.
arithmetic.shownWorking: Same bands, but the first step is 6.18: 75 x 6.18 = 463.50, and the remaining bands are unchanged. 3509.12 - 394.50 + 463.50 = 3578.12.

question: State the exact energy-charge effect of the 4 June order relative to the 3 June order, across the whole consumption range, and say precisely which parts of C1 and C2 are wrong.
